counterexample.constraintsExplanation: n=2 is in 1..100; exactly n binary rows of length n. A flip applies to a whole column shared by every row; clean means all ones.
counterexample.mathematicalDerivation: One common column-flip mask f cleans row r exactly when r XOR f is all ones, so f must equal the complement of r. Two simultaneously cleanable rows must therefore be identical. The actual row multiplicities are {'10': 1, '01': 1}; their maximum is 1, attained by complementing row 10. Complementary but nonidentical rows need different masks and cannot both be cleaned.
